title: Delhi police suspect murder-suicide after Malayali techie & wife found dead in Gurugram flat; he sent contact info before death
content: Kozhikode: Mystery shrouds the tragic deaths of a young Malayali couple whose bodies were found inside a flat near Gurugram, Haryana, on Thursday. Police suspect that 30-year-old man murdered his 28-year-old wife before taking his own life. The deceased have been identified as Muhammed Aslam, a native of Pullavoor, Koduvally in Kozhikode district, and his wife Farhana, a native of Nediyiruppu, Kondotty in Malappuram district. The couple, who do not have children, previously lived and worked in Bengaluru before relocating to Gurugram a few months ago. Aslam was employed as an IT professional at a private firm in Gurugram. The tragic incident came to light when the couple was found dead inside a flat at Marina Society in Sector 68, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Badshahpur police station. Upon receiving information, local authorities and police rushed to the scene to complete inquest proceedings. The bodies were subsequently shifted to the mortuary at Sadar Bazar in Delhi for post-mortem examinations, after which they are set to be handed over to relatives who have arrived from Kerala. Badshahpur Police Inspector Manoj told Onmanorama that investigators suspect Aslam killed his wife before dying by suicide. "The exact motive behind the murder and suicide is not yet clear. We have launched a detailed investigation into the matter, and further information will be revealed only after the inquiry and post-mortem reports are finalised," Inspector Manoj said. According to initial reports, prior to the tragic incident, Aslam had allegedly sent an email to his company's employer containing contact numbers for his father and the landlord. Relatives of Farhana have already reached Gurugram, and the bodies are expected to be brought back to Kerala for final rites. Childhood friend and neighbour rejects suicide theory The sudden tragedy has left family, friends, and neighbours in profound disbelief. Muhammed Unais, a childhood friend and neighbour of Farhana, firmly stated that there is no possibility of Farhana taking her own life, describing her as someone who led a happy and fulfilled life. "Farhana always had a warm and pleasant personality, and the couple always seemed made for each other in their outlook on life. They loved to travel, sharing photos of their trips across the country on social media, and they constantly persuaded me and my wife, Faseela, to join them. Hearing the news of her death was an absolute shock," Unais said. Sharing details about their background, Unais noted that both Farhana and Aslam held well-paying jobs in Bengaluru, coming from well-educated, professional families. Farhana has a sister who works as a teacher and a brother who manages Civil Services coaching sessions. After completing her BTech, Farhana secured a job in Bengaluru, where Aslam was also working as an IT professional. "We never knew of any problems between Farhana and Aslam, and we cannot believe there was any dispute between them. They were a true model of a happily married couple to us," Unais shared. He added that Farhana had recently contacted his wife to invite them on a pleasure trip, emphasising that both Farhana and Aslam were deeply religious, making the thought of suicide extremely difficult for them.
